eventMetadata.context_description: Recent powerful cold fronts sweeping the Western Cape on May 11-12, triggering South African Weather Service (SAWS) orange-level warnings for disruptive heavy rainfall, damaging winds up to gale-force, and storm surges, have ushered in a cool maritime air mass, anchoring trader consensus around 18-19°C maxima well below May's climatological average of ~20°C. SAWS detailed forecast calls for a 17°C high on May 14 with partly cloudy skies and light winds, but international model ensembles (ECMWF, GFS) exhibit a 17-19°C spread, with trader sentiment—evident in 19°C's slim 41.5% edge over 18°C at 35.5%—favoring marginal warming from high-pressure ridging and enhanced solar heating post-frontal clearance. Differentiating factors include model variances in boundary-layer mixing and residual low-cloud persistence; updated SAWS advisories and 12Z model runs expected today could tip the balance.

eventMetadata.context_description: Trader consensus on Polymarket reflects tight uncertainty in short-range forecasts for Guangzhou's May 14 high temperature, with 29°C (22.5%), 28°C (20.5%), and 30°C (18.5%) leading amid an incoming rain system. Recent National Hurricane Center analogs aren't applicable here, but updated ensemble models from sources like ECMWF and GFS, aggregated in forecasts from AccuWeather and TimeandDate, project highs of 28-29°C under overcast skies and 91-95% precipitation probability, a drop from May 12's 31°C amid stray thunderstorms. Differentiating factors include potential breaks in persistent cloud cover allowing brief solar heating to push toward 30°C, versus widespread rain suppressing peaks near 28°C; high humidity (80%+) and light ESE winds further temper extremes. New model runs and China Meteorological Administration updates expected within 24 hours could refine this before resolution at Baiyun Airport station.

Differentiating factors include potential midday cloud breaks boosting solar insolation for 36-37°C spikes, versus afternoon sea breeze or convection capping at 33-34°C, amplified by urban heat island effects at the airport. Historical May averages hover at 34°C, but recent days hit 36.7°C at nearby Science Garden amid high heat indices over 42°C. Daily PAGASA updates and global model runs (GFS, ECMWF) overnight could refine peak timing uncertainties.
